diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $P_{\no}$ is the orthonormal projector onto $\Y_\no$.

issues.failure_explanation: The error of F_no^# is not bounded by ||(I-P_no)F||. Since F_no^# x = F P_{X_no} x (where P_{X_no} projects onto X_no), the error is ||F(I-P_{X_no})x||. In general ||F(I-P_{X_no})|| is not bounded by ||(I-P_no)F||. For example, in R^2 let X_no=span(e1), F(e1)=e1, F(e2)=e1+e2; then ||(I-P_no)F||=1 but for x=e2, ||F x - F_no^# x||=sqrt(2)>1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace nu_no = ||(I-P_no)F|| by ||F(I-P_{X_no})|| (or bound the error directly by ||F(I-P_{X_no})||). This preserves convergence for compact F.
issues.overall_effect: The bound on ||F x - F_no^# x||_Y in cor:rate is false, so the estimate rho_n <= nu_no + no q r and the expression in th:linear using nu_no are not established. The actual error term is ||F(I-P_{X_no})||.
issues.title: Corollary cor:rate uses wrong projection for F_no^# error
issues.why_classification: The wrong projection can be corrected locally; the main rate structure and convergence for compact F survive with a different error term.

issues.failure_explanation: From |a-b|<=q and ||y-c||<=r one cannot conclude ||a y - b c||<=q r. The cross terms a(y-c) and (a-b)y are not controlled by q r. The correct bound involves q||y|| + r||b||. Thus the estimate ||F_no^# x - tilde F_n[x]|| <= no q r is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound no q r by a correct bound such as no(q+r) (under boundedness assumptions on uly and the branch approximations), or add assumptions that make the product bound valid.
issues.overall_effect: The approximation error estimate rho_n <= nu_no + no q r is invalid, so the rate in th:linear expressed as O(sqrt(delta)+sqrt(nu_no+no q r)) is unsupported. The example's rate no^{-1-p/2} is also unsupported; the correct rate would involve q+r.
issues.title: Corollary cor:rate incorrectly bounds product approximation error by no q r
issues.why_classification: The claimed rate is materially better than what the assumptions support; repairing requires a new error analysis and may worsen the rate, so the central approximation guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follow easily from the Rellich-Kondrachov theorem (see \cite[Theorem 6.2]{Ada75}), which states that the embedding $H^s(\Omega_\X) \hookrightarrow C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$ is compact for $s > \frac{m}{2}$, and from \cite[Theorem 4 \& Theorem 5]{TiaHon95}.
assume that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited Chen-Chen theorems require F to be continuous on a compact subset of C. Here F is assumed continuous in the stronger H^s topology and dom(F) compact in C. The compact embedding H^s into C does not imply a C-compact set is H^s-compact, nor does H^s-continuity imply C-continuity on such a set. A counterexample: let dom(F)={0} union {x_n} with x_n->0 in C but ||x_n||_{H^s}->infinity, and set F(x_n)=1, F(0)=0. Then F is H^s-continuous but not C-continuous, so no continuous neural functional can uniformly approximate F on this C-compact set.

failure_location.quote: suppose that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume dom(F) is compact in H^s (so the H^s and C topologies coincide on dom(F)) or assume F is continuous in C and apply the Chen-Chen theorems directly.
issues.overall_effect: The universal approximation theorems th:functional apx and th:operatorapx are not established under the stated hypotheses. Consequently, the Sobolev-space neural operator approximation and its applications (e.g., the a-example with neural operators) lack a valid foundation.
issues.title: Sobolev approximation theorems use mismatched compactness hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The central Sobolev approximation results fail as stated; a repair requires changing hypotheses or providing a new proof, with major consequences for the paper's applications.

issues.failure_explanation: In eq:deeponet the branch net evaluates x at bs_j, where j indexes the trunk basis. The sum over l therefore only multiplies the same value x(bs_j) by different weights, collapsing to one effective sensor per j. The network cannot represent functionals requiring N_l distinct sensor points. The theorem th:operatorapx claims existence of points bs_l and weights w_{j,k,l} such that F_n from eq:deeponet approximates any continuous operator, which is false for the displayed formula. The theorem text and coefficient count also conflict (text says bs_l, count assumes bs_j).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change x(bs_j) to x(bs_l) in eq:deeponet and adjust the parameter count to include N_l m sensor coordinates (or make sensor points shared as intended).
issues.overall_effect: The universal approximation theorem for operators th:operatorapx is false as stated; the L^2 approximation theorem and applications relying on it are unsupported.
issues.title: Neural operator definition misindexes branch sensor points, defeating operator universal approximation
issues.why_classification: The intended universal approximation result survives after a local correction to the definition and parameter count, but the written theorem is false.

issues.failure_explanation: Because x is extended by zero, if x in H^k(Omega_X) does not vanish at the boundary, the extension has a jump and is not in H^k(R^m). Mollification then produces a boundary layer. For example, x=1 on (0,1) satisfies x in H^2 but ||x_xi-x||_{L^2}=O(sqrt(xi)), not O(xi^2). Thus the estimate ||x_xi-x||_{H^s}<=C xi^{k-s} ||x||_{H^k} is false for general x in H^k.

failure_location.quote: For all $s \leq k$ and $\x \in H^k(\Omega_\X)$, $$\norms{\x_\xi-\x}_{H^s} \leq C\xi^{k-s}\norms{\x}_{H^k} = \mathcal{O}(\xi^{k-s})\;.$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a Sobolev extension operator that preserves H^k (not zero extension) or assume x in H_0^k; then the estimate holds. For the c-example this changes the mollification construction.
